name: Space
facts: A day on Venus is longer than its year.
Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tonnes on Earth.
Footprints left on the Moon by Apollo astronauts can last millions of years because there is no wind to erase them.
Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
Jupiter is so big that all the other planets in the Solar System could fit inside it.
Saturn is less dense than water, so it would float in a big enough bathtub.
By many estimates, there are more stars in the observable universe than grains of sand on all of Earth's beaches.
The International Space Station circles Earth about every 90 minutes.
Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the Solar System, about two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.
Space is completely silent because there is no air to carry sound.
One million Earths could fit inside the Sun.
Uranus spins on its side, with its axis tilted about 98 degrees.
The Andromeda galaxy is the farthest object most people can see with the naked eye, about 2.5 million light-years away.
Mercury has almost no atmosphere, so temperatures swing from about 430°C in the day to about -180°C at night.
A year on Neptune lasts about 165 Earth years.
The Moon is slowly moving away from Earth, by about 3.8 centimetres a year.
Astronauts can grow a few centimetres taller in space because their spines stretch without gravity.
Mars looks red because its surface is rich in iron oxide, which is rust.
The Great Red Spot on Jupiter is a storm bigger than Earth.
Venus is the hottest planet in the Solar System, even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.
Light from the most distant galaxies we can see left them more than 13 billion years ago.
Halley's Comet passes by Earth about every 76 years; it will next be visible in 2061.
In 2019, scientists released the first image of a black hole, at the centre of the galaxy M87.
Saturn's rings are mostly made of ice, with some rock and dust.
Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on 12 April 1961.
